- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.2) and forecast is rising, cap the forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average to prevent false momentum.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion (price dropping from peak), adjust forecast downward by 2–5% to reflect exhaustion.  
- If sentiment is volatile (fluctuating >0.3) and forecast is erratic, smooth the forecast curve by averaging 3–5 consecutive points to reduce noise.  
- When sentiment is consistently positive but price is trending down, reduce forecast slope by 10–15% to account for sentiment-driven overcorrection.  
- For forecasts with large overshoots (>10% above true value), apply a “lag correction” by subtracting 1–2% per day for the next 3–5 days to reflect delayed market reaction.
